findings.title: Naive sentence-boundary regex clips 22.37% (85,518 / 382,286) of opening previews at judicial titles, initials, citations, and statutory abbreviations while falsely setting partial_sentence=false
findings.root_cause: In pipeline_v2/navigation/core.py line 35, _opening() searches for the first punctuation match via re.search(r'[.!?](?=\s|$)', text[pos:stop]). In Canadian Federal Court decisions, paragraphs and unnumbered blocks routinely open with or contain judicial titles ('Pinard, J.', 'Mandamin, J.', 'Teitelbaum, J.', 'O\'Keefe, J.'), honorifics/initials ('Mr.', 'Ms.', 'Dr.', 'M.', 'John H.', 'Charlotte M.', 'A.', '1.'), statutory abbreviations ('s.', 'ss.', 'para.', 'paras.', 'art.'), or reporter citations ('F.C.', 'R.S.C.', 'P.C.'). The regex stops at the period after the abbreviation, producing a 2-to-30 character fragment that omits the entire legal proposition of the paragraph. In addition, line 128 computes partial_sentence as bool(b < end and text[b - 1] not in '.!?'), which evaluates to False whenever text[b - 1] == '.', falsely certifying 100% of these mid-sentence abbreviation clips as complete sentences.

findings.agent_impact: In M4 map views, the agent relies on unit previews to decide which paragraphs to open under a strict reading budget. When 22.37% of opening previews are truncated at 'Pinard, J.', 'Mr.', 's.', or '1.', the map view conceals the subject matter of the paragraph (especially paragraph [1] which states the nature of the judicial review and outcome, and numbered list items or statutory citations) and misleads any consumer inspecting partial_sentence=false.
findings.minimal_fix_direction: Update _opening() and partial_sentence detection in pipeline_v2/navigation/core.py to skip common legal/honorific/initial/enumeration abbreviations (e.g., ', J.', 'J.A.', 'Prothonotary', 'Mr.', 'Ms.', 'Mrs.', 'Dr.', 'M.', 'Mme.', 's.', 'ss.', 'para.', 'paras.', 'art.', 'v.', 'c.', 'No.', 'R.S.C.', 'S.C.', 'F.C.', 'F.T.R.', 'D.L.R.', single-letter initials '[A-Z]\.', and list markers '^\d+\.' or '^[A-Za-z]\.') and require a minimum substantive length (or continue to the next sentence boundary up to max_chars=240) when a period is followed by a colon, lowercase token, section number, or surname.

findings.title: Anchor preview window starts at unit byte 0 (before opening[0]), preventing merge with opening in 31,352 units, emitting redundant substring previews in 56,996 units, and crowding out deeper anchors in 11,505 units
findings.root_cause:
In pipeline_v2/navigation/core.py lines 103-116, _opening() skips the leading paragraph marker ('[15]
') or placeholder-only lines so opening[0] > start. However, for any anchor near the beginning of the unit, line 104 computes left = max(start, a - radius), which reaches back to start (including '[15]
'). Line 110 then checks 'not (overlapping[2] == "opening" and opening and lo < opening[0])', explicitly refusing to merge the anchor window with the opening window whenever left < opening[0]. Furthermore, line 113 ('overlapping[0] <= left and right <= overlapping[1]') only checks whether opening contains anchor, not whether anchor contains opening. Consequently, both previews are emitted in the 2-slot map budget (max_display=2): one with '[15]
...' and one identical substring without '[15]
', which consumes the second display slot and prevents any second or third anchor later in the paragraph from getting a preview.

findings.agent_impact: Wastes 1 of the 2 map preview slots per unit on a near-duplicate substring in 56,996 units and actively hides a deeper citation/quote-cue anchor in 11,505 units (visible_anchor_count drops from 2+ to 1 even though the second preview slot was available).
findings.minimal_fix_direction: Clamp the anchor window start to content_start = opening[0] if opening else start (so anchor windows do not pull in the leading '[N]\r\n' marker or skipped placeholder lines), remove the 'not (overlapping[2] == "opening" and opening and lo < opening[0])' block, and check two-way containment or high overlap when merging/deduplicating opening and anchor windows so the second preview slot is preserved for distinct deeper anchors.

findings.title: Leading placeholder-only line filter in _opening() fails when line contains stray punctuation/brackets alongside <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED>
findings.root_cause: In pipeline_v2/navigation/core.py lines 26-27, _opening() skips leading lines only when PLACEHOLDER.sub('', value).strip() is empty ('if value and not PLACEHOLDER.sub("", value).strip(): cursor = line_end; continue'). In 932 content units across the corpus, header or body lines consist solely of <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED> tags plus stray punctuation such as ')', '.', ',', ';', or '[' (e.g., '<FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED> )  <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED>' or '<FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED>.'). Because PLACEHOLDER.sub('', value).strip() leaves ')' or '.', the line is treated as substantive opening text.
findings.reproduction_command: & .venv/Scripts/python.exe -c "from pathlib import Path; from pipeline_v2.navigation import M2NavigationStore; s = M2NavigationStore(Path('.'), Path('pipeline_v2/artifacts/m2_navigation_20261105_v1')); print(s.map('081945.txt', start_ord=1, end_ord=1)['units']); print(s.map('001867.txt', start_ord=1, end_ord=1)['units'])"
findings.agent_impact: In 932 units, _opening() starts on a line containing only suppressed placeholders and stray punctuation instead of advancing to the first line with alphanumeric words (or returning None when the entire unit has no alphanumeric content).
findings.minimal_fix_direction: Check whether any alphanumeric character (any(ch.isalnum() for ch in PLACEHOLDER.sub('', value))) remains on the line after stripping placeholders, rather than checking only .strip() != ''.

findings.title: Hard codepoint-offset cuts in anchor preview windows slice adjacent <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED> tags and cap long quote cues at 120 chars when preceded by 120 chars of pre-anchor context
findings.root_cause: Lines 104-105 compute left = max(start, a - 120) and right = min(end, left + 240, b + 120). Because left and right are raw codepoint offsets, (1) when another <FRAGMENT_SUPPRESSED> tag lies near left + 240, right cuts through the middle of that tag (e.g. ending with '<FRAGMENT_S' or '<'), and (2) when a quote-introduction cue (a, b) is longer than 120 chars and occurs at least 120 chars into the unit, allocating 120 chars before 'a' leaves only 120 chars of the 240-char budget for the cue itself. Note that M2 honestly records visibility='partial', fully_visible=False, and source_cue_fully_visible=False in all such cases.

findings.title: Conservative paragraph_role ('unknown' on 355,736 / 356,973 paragraphs) and language_region preservation without heuristic voice guessing; deferred tokenizer/chunk readiness flags remain 'not_ready'
findings.root_cause: By design of M1 and M2 contracts, only paragraphs immediately following an observed local quote-introduction cue (1,237 paragraphs) receive paragraph_role='quoted' with quote_extent_beyond_this_unit_unresolved; all other 355,736 paragraphs retain paragraph_role='unknown' with paragraph_ownership_unresolved rather than guessing judicial vs party-submission voice. Similarly, 55 marker-only paragraphs (e.g., '[2]' in 000841.txt p000007) have preview_absence_reason='no_meaningful_opening_or_anchor', and token_count is null across all units until embedding/agent tokenizers are locked.
findings.reproduction_command: & .venv/Scripts/python.exe -c "from pathlib import Path; from pipeline_v2.navigation import M2NavigationStore; s = M2NavigationStore(Path('.'), Path('pipeline_v2/artifacts/m2_navigation_20261105_v1')); print(s.open('000841.txt', 'p000007', expand='neighbors'))"
findings.agent_impact: Safe by contract: when an agent calls open(handle, expand='neighbors'), the parent plus previous/next units and intervening headings resolve whether a paragraph is a party submission, statutory block quote, or judicial holding without risking false role attribution in the index.
findings.minimal_fix_direction: None required in M2; keep conservative provenance and uncertainty flags as designed.
